CAT.rationale: CAT's fundamental health is genuinely strong — Q1 2026 revenue +22.2% YoY, EPS +30.2% YoY, record $63B backlog, expanding Energy & Transportation margins (16.4% to 26.3% over 5 years), and a durable franchise with 150+ dealers and 1.6M connected assets. However, the valuation has become deeply disconnected from earnings power. The trailing PE has expanded 2.6x in 12 months (16.89x to 43.86x), placing CAT at the 96th percentile of its own valuation history. The 2.3% earnings yield sits well below the 4.45% 10-year Treasury yield, and the stock has gained 161% from its 365-day low while EPS grew only 30.2%. Net margins have compressed from 15.7% historical to 13.3% latest, and leverage has risen to 4.12x D/E. Tariff headwinds of $2.2-2.4B for 2026 and insider selling in May 2026 add near-term risk. The potential $1.5-1.8B Supreme Court tariff refund is a credible positive catalyst, but it is not enough to justify a 43.86x PE on a cyclical industrial. Mean reversion to even 25x PE implies ~43% downside. The risk/reward is asymmetrically negative at this valuation — all three pillars (fundamentals stretched by valuation, extreme vs own history, and limited near-term catalysts to justify the multiple) point strongly negative.
